site_description: Working through Godot tasks, one GIF at a time.

tasks.title: 1. Add TileMapLayer
tasks.description: Getting started by adding a 2D Scene root node and a TileMapLayer node to create the level. Call the root node 'Level1' and the TileMapLayer 'Ground'

tasks.title: 2. Add a Tileset
tasks.description: Add a Tileset resource for the TileMapLayer. Note: you first need to have downloaded your tileset image.

tasks.title: 3. Add Physics to Tileset
tasks.description: Add collision properties to the Tileset so that players don't fall through your blocks

tasks.title: 4. Painting the Level
tasks.description: Using the TileMapLayer's painting tools to create a level.

tasks.title: 5. Adding a Test Character
tasks.description: Adding a simple test character to the level to test out the collision properties

tasks.title: 6. Export Spritesheet from Piskel
tasks.description: Once you have created your pixel art character in Piskel you need to export it as a spritesheet to use in Godot. Important: choose the 'Export' option, then choose 'Spritesheet file export'

tasks.title: 7. Create AnimatedSprite2D
tasks.description: Create an AnimatedSprite2D node for your character and add the spritesheet you exported from Piskel as a SpriteFrames resource. Be sure to click 'Autorun' on the animation so that it plays when you run the scene.

tasks.title: 8. Modify Collision Shape
tasks.description: Modify the CollisionShape2D of your character to fit the new sprite. Adjust the texture processing to 'Nearest' to preserve the pixel art look

tasks.title: 9. Add Script to Character
tasks.description: Rename the CharacterBody2D as 'Player'. Add a script to your character to give it some basic movement. Use the provided default script template to get started

tasks.title: 10. Create Collectible Area2D Node
tasks.description: Create a collectible item for the player to collect. Create a new Area2D node with an AnimatedSprite2D and CollisionShape2D as children. Use a simple circle shape for the collision shape and a spritesheet (like the coin image provided) for the collectible.

tasks.title: 11. Save Collectible as Scene
tasks.description: Save your collectible as a separate scene so that you can easily reuse it throughout your level.

tasks.title: 12. Add Script to Collectible
tasks.description: Add a script to your collectible to make it disappear when the player collects it and emit the 'coin_collected' signal. (See coin.gd code for reference). Add the player to the 'player' group.

tasks.title: 13. Track Score
tasks.description: Connect the 'coin_collected' signal to the player. Add a score variable to your player script so you can increment the score when the player collects a coin.
